item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=artificial+intelligence+agency+accountability+decision+consequences+responsibility&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.4018/979-8-2600-2870-4.ch007\", \"title\": [\"Determining Responsibility for Artificial Intelligence-Based Security Decision Making\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The chapter discusses the determination of who is responsible when artificial intelligence is used for security decision making within complex organizational environments. It looks at how accountability is shared among system designers, vendors, deployers, and human operators when AI-driven tools are used to influence detection actions, prioritization, and response. The chapter investigates legal principles explaining the relationship between control, foreseeability, and duty of care, along with regulatory requirements for human oversight and governance. It also examines issues related to automation bias, black-box models, and extended decision chains that involve Security Operations Centers and third parties. Special focus is given to documentation, role clarity, chain of command for escalation, and auditability as means of defining responsibility. Through combining a legal perspective with security operational practice, the chapter outlines a system for determining responsibility, handling liability, and making defensible decisions in AI-assisted security systems.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.4018/979-8-2600-2870-4.ch007\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 7, 9]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4018/979-8-3693-4099-8.ch007\", \"title\": [\"Artificial Intelligence-Driven Corporate Social Responsibility Reporting\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>In a global environment where stakeholders believe ethical company practices, CSR reporting is vital for transparency. Traditional reporting methods often fail due to human data management, inaccuracies, and lack of real-time insights. AI has given businesses novel opportunities to rethink CSR strategy and reporting. This chapter examines how AI-driven systems might improve transparency and accountability through automated data gathering, better analytics, and insights that encourage corporate responsibility.
